Change has been successfully rebased and submitted as 88dfc5b88094b54d6443c2ec5154f8a1f3e70693
is there really a need for a malloc here?

There was in one variation of this patch, but yes, this isn't needed now that getConfiguration has been ported to take string_view.

Fixed
same here. If a vector is required here, can we update it to take a range or iterators or span?

This is different, but I've moved this to be constexpr std::array.  getConfiguration (as of the patch a few days ago) now supports span of string_view.

Fixed
This seems like a bug. Why are emplacing this when we've already constructed it with the same thing.
Yes.... this is a bug.  Fixed.
same here, why can't we do this at constexpr?

Two answers to "why not"
1. We don't on master today, so I made the most surgical change here I could.
2. I don't know of a way to convert a std::array<std::pair<...>> into an array of string view at compile time (although it might be possible now that we have constexpr vector in c++23)

If you do, please give me a code snippet, and I can do that.

https://godbolt.org/z/aEP3TaYb5

this seems to roughly do it with index_sequences.
follow on is fine, also this is relatively advanced template-fu. If we think that readability is preferred, I won't die on this hill.

This also requires the compiler to generate N template instantiations of extractFirstImpl afaict, maybe we don't care about that, since its in a cpp file, but its the sort of thing that leads to compile time bloat.

> this is relatively advanced template-fu

Exactly.  For code that's a single malloc of a small data structure done only at configure time, and not in the hot loop, I have a strong preference for what's here given it's simpler to read and reason about.  I do suspect that you could do this in a consteval method and keep it both simple and constexpr, but that's a follow on.

If this were in a hot loop and we should show that mallocs were causing performance issues, I'd be all for template-fu.
Yep, that's about what I'd expect.  Can follow on with another patch to propose that (unless you want to push it)
same here, this seems to be known at compile time?
Done

not really related to this review, but we should probably handle stuff like this in the register_property function, not at the call site. If the function needs a certain lifetime for its parameters, it should enforce it, IMO.

register_property is in sdbusplus. We could maybe handle this, but std::string_view is a weird case, because the value is functionally const.  All the other properties assume that the property could be read/write, even if we don't register the handler.

Could be fixed.
Done
